chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from his father, saying: Al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), said:

The requirements of people in this perishable world are four: Wealth, comfort, little concern, and honor. As for wealth, it is found in contentment; so whoever seeks it in the abundance of property, will not find it. As for comfort, it is found in light carrying; so whoever seeks it in its heaviness, will not find it. As for little concern, it is found in little occupation; so whoever seeks it with an abundance of it, will not find it. As for honor, it is found in serving the Creator; so whoever seeks it in serving the created, will not find it.
ai.seo_question: What are the four true requirements of people in the perishable world according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a profound spiritual redefinition of four common worldly desires, shifting the focus from external accumulation to internal state. He teaches that true wealth is found in contentment (*qana'ah*), comfort in a light burden (*khifat al-haml*), peace of mind in minimal occupation, and honor in serving the Creator rather than being subservient to created beings. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on inner purification (*tazkiyah*) and aligns with the concept that the ultimate goal of human existence is nearness to God, not material accumulation.
